name: alp-luachra

attributes.attribute: driven out with salty food and a stream

sources: Hyde, Douglas. Beside the Fire: A Collection of Irish Gaelic Folk Stories. London: David Nutt, 1890, 47.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The alp-luachra is a water sprite. A person could swallow it by accident, and it caused endless trouble. It gave the victim stomach ailments until it was coaxed back out of the mouth. Some said the trouble began when a person swallowed a newt. The newt, a small amphibian, changed into an alp-luachra inside the body. To drive it out, the victim ate salty food without washing it down with drink. The victim then slept beside a stream. Dying of thirst, the alp-luachra leapt from the mouth and back into the water.
objective: Record the alp-luachra, an Irish water sprite.
key_results: Show the accidental swallow and the salty-food cure.
evidence: Monaghan 2003, s.v. alp-luachra; Koch 2006, s.v. Sprite
